## 1B.10 Research Note: Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023

**Working judgment:** **More dangerous than inherited.** The strongest 2023 signals are cumulative escalation: New START suspension, tactical nuclear deployment in Belarus, continued ZNPP volatility, and wider offensive cyber/bio opacity. The main pro-restraint items are declaratory or crisis-containment measures, not a durable de-escalation.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 31.03.2023 г. № 229`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 31 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia’s updated foreign-policy concept says it will support strategic stability, arms control, nonproliferation, and reductions in nuclear risk. This is the clearest pro-restraint evidence in 2023, but it is doctrine rather than operational de-escalation.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Title:** `IAEA Director General Grossi Travels to Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant Next Week`  
  **Publisher:** IAEA  
  **Date:** 27 Feb 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/iaea-director-general-grossi-travels-to-zaporizhzhya-nuclear-power-plant-next-week](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/iaea-director-general-grossi-travels-to-zaporizhzhya-nuclear-power-plant-next-week)  
  **Claim-level summary:** The IAEA said it was trying to reduce accident risk at Zaporizhzhya, keep expert rotations going, and protect the plant during war. This is a limited positive signal that Russia engaged a formal safety channel, but it reflects crisis management, not a safer overall posture.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.10`, `1B.3`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`

- **Title:** `Russia Suspends New START`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters / Gulf News  
  **Date:** 21 Feb 2023  
  **URL:** [https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764](https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin announced suspension of Russia’s participation in New START and threatened renewed nuclear testing. This is one of the clearest 2023 moves that made the existential-risk posture more dangerous than before.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.10`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`

- **Title:** `Russia signs deal to deploy tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, says they stay under its control`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 25 May 2023  
  **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/](https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia formalized deployment of tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus while saying Moscow would retain control over them. This widened coercive leverage and command complexity, pushing the posture toward greater danger.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.3`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`

- **Title:** `Putin says Russia positions nuclear bombs in Belarus as warning to West`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 16 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-positions-nuclear-bombs-in-belarus-as-warning-to-west-3107500](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-positions-nuclear-bombs-in-belarus-as-warning-to-west-3107500)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin said the first tactical nuclear warheads had been delivered to Belarus as a warning that the West could not inflict a strategic defeat on Russia. That is direct evidence of using nuclear leverage to support coercive wartime aims, not of making the posture safer.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`

- **Title:** `Update 146 – IAEA Director General Statement on Situation in Ukraine`  
  **Publisher:** IAEA  
  **Date:** 13 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-146-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-146-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine)  
  **Claim-level summary:** The IAEA said the situation at Zaporizhzhya was volatile and unpredictable, with military activity delaying expert rotation and complicating safety work. This supports the view that Putin’s 2023 posture left a major nuclear risk environment more dangerous.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.10`, `1B.3`, `1B.8`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2023 evidence that Putin made the country’s existential-risk posture materially safer in a structural sense, such as restoring arms-control inspections, reducing forward nuclear exposure, or creating durable transparency in cyber or bio domains. The pro-restraint evidence is mainly declaratory or crisis-containment.

### Bottom line

**More dangerous than inherited.** The year ends with more nuclear leverage, weaker arms-control posture, and persistent multi-domain risk, despite some formal safety language and limited crisis-management engagement.
